name: Aubrey Farah
life: “I still remember apologizing to somebody I had paid to be polite.” On Thursday, near Juniper Street, Aubrey knows which of the west-side porches has a seat in the shade.
voice: I accused my carer of mixing up the bags. I am taking the apology to her home on foot.
appearance: Away from the heat of the kitchen, look for a cropped bottle-green coat and a comb in a sleeve sewn into the lining. Aubrey has a crooked front tooth visible when laughing, with soft white hair brushed sideways. Aubrey gives a little nod before asking a hard question during a conversation.
personality: Aubrey always notices who paid for the last round. In a group that can be a kindness or a small tyranny, and Aubrey is trying to tell the difference before the bill arrives.
agenda: To deliver an apology to the carer at home.
family: Cyrus Cole is Aubrey’s younger relative by marriage. Aubrey sets the time to leave. Cyrus picks the meeting place. It lets them stay close without turning a family visit into the loss of an entire day. They have both had stretches when that distinction mattered. Asked about *The aquarium*, Cyrus says, “One fish has a crooked jaw. It needs its food dropped on the left.”
connections: Ruth Farah. A house call to apologize becomes an opportunity to return the mended iron rest.

reactions.situation: An elderly tenant wants to iron the collar personally
reactions.response: Aubrey lets the tenant do the collar at a safe height and takes the heavier laundry.

reactions.situation: A frightened child is waiting outside a shuttered shop
reactions.response: Aubrey asks the nearest shop worker to stay too, then talks about ordinary things until the child can explain who is late.

reactions.situation: If somebody tries to repay an old favor all at once
reactions.response: Aubrey suggests a smaller gesture they can repeat without hardship.
